_note: Long Book candidate list. Hand-curated claims checklist: every claim has a status and primary-source links; reviewed 2026-10-19 (Grok Bot). Statuses: shipped (live on mainnet), testnet, roadmap (planned, no code on mainnet), marketing (claim with no matching technical source), verified / partly / not-verified (for buyback numbers vs DefiLlama/on-chain). Metrics are pulled by research/longbook/longbook.py; nothing here is a price target.

candidates.thesis: First large L1 with opt-in NIST ML-DSA-65 account signatures live on mainnet (July 2026); rotatable access keys make migration cheap.

claims.claim: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) transaction signatures and access keys
claims.note: Protocol v85, neard 2.13. Opt-in; Ed25519/secp256k1 not deprecated. NEP-645 still marked Draft.
Explicitly out of scope of the first milestone; consensus stays classical.
Gated separately from the transaction feature in nearcore docs; activation on mainnet not confirmed in the 2.13 notes.

claims.claim: Quantum-safe custody of other chains' assets via Chain Signatures / Intents
claims.note: Chain Signatures MPC and the destination chains remain elliptic-curve; only the NEAR account key is PQ.

risks: PQ is opt-in: most accounts stay Ed25519 until users rotate
Consensus/validator crypto still classical
Chain fees are small (~$1.3M/yr DefiLlama) so the token has no revenue support; it is a narrative + L1 adoption bet
Inflationary staking issuance (~5%/yr nominal, part burned via fees)
thesisBreak: ML-DSA rolled back or a critical bug found in the PQ path
No validator/consensus PQ work shipped by end-2027 (roadmap slips)
Price makes a new 1y low after a sentiment 'euphoric' reading (narrative exhausted)

candidates.thesis: Longest live PQ track record: Falcon-signed State Proofs since 2022 and native Falcon-1024 accounts on mainnet since Aug 2026.

claims.note: Every 256 rounds, signed by a stake supermajority.
Consensus v42 in go-algorand v5.0.0; existing accounts can rekey. Higher min fee (3,000 microAlgo).
Consensus participation keys and VRF are still classical.

risks: Very low fee revenue (DefiLlama ~$6K/yr) and low on-chain demand
Foundation-driven ecosystem; adoption has lagged its tech for years
Consensus still classical
thesisBreak: PQ multisig / consensus milestones slip past 2027
Falcon implementation flaw
Daily volume and listings shrink (delisting risk)

candidates.thesis: Purpose-built PQ chain: XMSS mainnet since 2018; QRL 2.0 (ML-DSA-87, EVM-like) on testnet, mainnet gated on audits.

claims.claim: QRL 1.x mainnet secured by hash-based XMSS signatures
claims.note: Proof-of-work chain, no smart contracts.

claims.claim: QRL 2.0 Zond: ML-DSA-87 accounts + validators, Hyperion/QRVM smart contracts
claims.note: Testnet V2. No mainnet date; audits & remediation 60% as of 2026-09-18.
Deferred to after 2.0 mainnet.

risks: Tiny liquidity and few listings (size must be small)
2.0 mainnet date not set; past roadmap targets slipped
No protocol revenue
No free price history beyond 365 days in the terminal (backtest excluded)
thesisBreak: Audit finds critical issues and mainnet slips into 2027 H2+
Major exchange delisting
Liquidity under $100K/day

candidates.thesis: Privacy coin with a concrete PQ migration path: Ironwood notes are quantum-recoverable since NU6.3 (Jul 2026). Not quantum-safe yet.

claims.note: False today: ZIP 2005 says it 'does not by itself make the protocol secure against quantum adversaries'.
NU6.3 at block 3,428,143. Only funds moved into Ironwood are covered; ZIP status Proposed.

claims.claim: Recovery Protocol (PQ spend of recoverable notes)
claims.note: Described 'in outline but not in detail'; not in consensus.

risks: Price already ran very far (see 1y drawdown / 200d multiple): late-cycle entry risk
Privacy-coin delisting / regulatory risk
Sapling/Orchard/transparent funds not recoverable unless moved
PoW issuance, no buyback
thesisBreak: Exchange delistings in a major market
Recovery Protocol work stalls (no ZIP progress in 12 months)
Shielded share falls back (terminal zec_shielded desk)

candidates.thesis: Credible PQ roadmap (ML-DSA-65 native accounts, SLH-DSA vaults) on a high-usage L1, but nothing PQ on mainnet yet.

claims.note: Core implementation built; audits underway.
Timelines 'remain open'.

risks: Large ongoing unlocks (only ~41% of 10B circulating per DefiLlama unlocks)
PQ is roadmap-only today
Validator set and token concentrated with foundation/insiders
thesisBreak: ML-DSA testnet misses end-2026
Unlock-driven supply growth with falling fees

candidates.thesis: Largest real buyback in crypto: ~all trading fees go to the Assistance Fund, which buys HYPE; validators voted (Dec 2025) to treat it as burned.

claims.claim: Trading fees buy HYPE via the Assistance Fund
claims.note: DefiLlama holdersRevenue = revenue; daily, no gaps in the terminal's buyburn study.

claims.claim: Assistance Fund HYPE is permanently burned
claims.note: Validator vote (85% stake) to treat 0xfefe...fe balance as burned; no transfer to a burn address.
Team tokens vest monthly after the Nov 2025 cliff; no official dated calendar, actual claims often below entitlement. Net change depends on claims vs buybacks.

risks: Team vesting (~24% of supply) adds supply monthly
Revenue is cyclical (perp volume); buybacks fall with volume
Validator/foundation concentration; L1 outage or exploit risk
Competition from other perp DEXs
thesisBreak: 30d holders revenue falls below 40% of its 1y monthly average
Assistance Fund policy changed away from buy-and-hold/burn
Major exploit or prolonged chain halt

candidates.thesis: Dominant on-chain options venue (~87% of on-chain premiums) buying back DRV weekly with 35% of fees, 50% after the Sep 2026 DIP.

claims.claim: 35% of applicable protocol fees to weekly DRV buybacks (50% passed Oct 2-5, 2026 Snapshot)
claims.note: Mechanism documented; DefiLlama does NOT track it (holdersRevenue = $0). Amounts are self-reported weekly.

claims.claim: Buybacks outpace emissions (16.6M burned vs 6.1M staking issuance YTD)
claims.note: Secondary source (Alea Research). Same report says circulating supply ROSE 17.1% this year: unlocks dwarf the burn. Not checked on-chain here.
35% of trailing-1y DefiLlama revenue is ~0.3% of market cap per year: tiny vs unlocks.

risks: Buyback is tiny relative to market cap and unlocks
Price-to-revenue very high
Thin DEX liquidity (~$255K main pool)
V3 migration risk (Derive Chain shutdown)
thesisBreak: Weekly buyback reports stop
Circulating supply grows >15%/yr while revenue flat
Options market share falls below 60%

candidates.thesis: Memecoin launchpad buying and burning PUMP with 50% of net revenue (locked for 1 year from Apr 2026) after burning 36% of supply.

claims.claim: 50% of net revenue to open-market PUMP buys, all burned
claims.note: Policy locked ~1 year (to ~Apr 2027). DefiLlama tracks holdersRevenue daily.
Replaced the earlier 'all revenue to buybacks' policy, which did not support price.

risks: Revenue tied to memecoin mania; collapses in a downturn
Large insider unlocks (DefiLlama unlocks: monthly insider cliffs)
Regulatory/legal exposure of the launchpad model
Policy has already changed once
thesisBreak: Buyback policy cut below 50% or ended early
30d revenue below 30% of its 1y monthly average
Counts toward the meme slice: exit if the meme slice exceeds its cap

candidates.thesis: Fee switch (UNIfication) live since Dec 2025: protocol fees can only be withdrawn by burning UNI (TokenJar/Firepit).

claims.claim: Protocol fees live; UNI burned via Firepit to access them
claims.note: DefiLlama holdersRevenue = revenue. v4 fees activated on selected pools in 2026.

risks: Fee capture is a small share of total Uniswap fees (most still go to LPs)
Fee tiers can be changed by governance
Competition (aggregators, other AMMs)
thesisBreak: Governance turns fees off or redirects them
30d holders revenue below 40% of its 1y monthly average

candidates.thesis: USDS issuer with large real revenue; Smart Burn Engine buys SKY, but most is redistributed to stakers and only ~5% is burned.

claims.note: Bought on market; DefiLlama holdersRevenue tracked.
Stage 2 split: 22.5% SKY staking rewards, 22.5% USDS rewards, 5% buy-and-burn. Burns of 2.86M and 7.37M SKY reported (Sep/Oct 2026). Net supply change ~0 over 12 months.

risks: Most 'buyback' is a staking subsidy, not a burn
USDS depends on RWA/crypto collateral yields
Complex governance; MKR->SKY migration history
thesisBreak: USDS supply falls >30% from peak
Burn share cut to 0

candidates.thesis: Solana AMM routing 12% of swap fees to open-market RAY buybacks for years; bought RAY is held, not burned.

claims.note: DefiLlama holdersRevenue tracked (one 286-day gap from 2024-07 in the terminal's study).
Held in a protocol wallet, not burned; governance could re-spend it.

risks: Bought RAY is not burned
Volume depends on Solana memecoin trading (PumpSwap competition)
Remaining unlocks (~22% of max per DefiLlama)
thesisBreak: Buyback wallet tokens sold or redistributed
Solana DEX share drops sharply

candidates.thesis: Tokenomics 3.0: fee-funded weekly buy-and-burn beats emissions; 37 straight deflationary months to Sep 2026.

claims.note: Sep 2026: 2.964M burned vs 0.653M minted (-0.70% supply). Target >=4%/yr reduction.

risks: BNB Chain concentration
Revenue falls with BSC memecoin volume
Emission policy is governance-set
thesisBreak: A month with net inflation
30d holders revenue below 40% of its 1y monthly average

rejected.why: Quantum: draft EIPs only (8141 etc.), L1 PQ 'could be completed by 2029'; roadmap-only. Buyback theme: EIP-1559 burn currently below issuance (terminal net_supply). Not a fit for either theme today.
SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s authenticator merged (PR #18300, Jan 2026) but feature flag 107 is not enabled on mainnet: code exists, nothing usable. Watch only.
Quantum: problem statements / research programs / opt-in vault programs only; no protocol-level PQ signatures on mainnet.
Buyback: DefiLlama holdersRevenue is $0 over the last 90 days (vs $17.5M over 1y): the program is paused or no longer tracked. Re-check before adding.
Buyback goes to a treasury ('litterbox'), not burned, and large future unlocks remain; weaker than RAY/CAKE on supply.
Buybacks held in treasury/reserve (not burned) or irregular (ASTER 50% uptime in the terminal's study).
Exchange/chain burns are real but centrally decided (quarterly announcements); OKB's program ended 2025-08. Not protocol-revenue buybacks in the DeFi sense.
